functions.name: batch-schedule-device-deletions
functions.description: Schedule asynchronous inventory removal for up to 100 devices and return the ordered per-device scheduling outcomes.

deviceUid.description: Device UID as reported by the Nexthink Collector.

deviceName.description: Nonblank Collector-reported device name paired with this UID.

items.description: Collector-reported identity pair for one device to schedule for inventory removal.

devices.description: Devices to queue for inventory removal, with a public maximum of 100; supplied order is retained.

FunctionInput_nexthink_batchscheduledevi.description: A single native batch of device inventory removals to schedule.

status.description: SCHEDULED means queued; INVALID means a malformed UID was skipped; FAILED means a downstream scheduling failure. Only SCHEDULED is successful queuing.

deviceUid.description: UID echoed for this submitted device.

deviceName.description: Name echoed for this submitted device.

items.description: The provider scheduling outcome for one submitted device.
Per-device outcomes in request order; no completed-deletion assertion.

status.description: Whole request accepted for scheduling; this does not establish success for every device.

requestId.description: Provider correlation identifier from x-request-id when available, for support diagnostics.

scheduledCount.description: Provider-reported number of devices successfully queued, not already deleted.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_batchscheduledev.description: Accepted batch scheduling results, not confirmation of completed inventory deletion.

tags.instructions: Use a suitable saved query through `execute-nql-query` to obtain each device's Collector-reported UID and name. Maximum 100 devices per call, or the deployment's smaller configured limit. Use `schedule-device-deletion` for one device. This queues inventory removal, not immediate deletion; reversibility is undocumented. Inspect each status, including FAILED, and retry only after checking whether a prior ambiguous request was applied.

functions.name: batch-trigger-remote-actions
functions.description: Request the same remote action with shared parameters on up to 100 devices. Return the provider's aggregate request ID without inventing per-device execution outcomes.

parameters.description: Shared script parameter values keyed by input ID; omitted means an empty map.

triggerInfo.description: Shared audit context for this request.

items.description: Nexthink Collector ID of a target device.

collectorIds.description: Distinct Nexthink Collector IDs, up to 100 per invocation; these are not device inventory UIDs.

remoteActionId.description: NQL ID of the one action to execute on all targets.

expiresInMinutes.description: Minutes before an offline target's unprocessed execution request expires; omitted uses the provider default.

FunctionInput_nexthink_batchtriggerremot.description: One remote action and shared parameters to submit for up to 100 distinct Collector IDs.

requestId.description: Aggregate request identifier for the spawned executions; not a per-device success report.

expiresInMinutes.description: Effective offline expiry in minutes, if returned.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_batchtriggerremo.description: Aggregate submission acknowledgement, without per-device acceptance or execution outcomes.

tags.instructions: Use `get-remote-action` to inspect the action and its parameters. Obtain Collector IDs with `execute-nql-query`. Use `trigger-remote-action` for one device. Maximum 100 devices per call. Submission does not establish device execution; scripts may modify devices, and replay may run them again. Use the returned requestId in a saved NQL execution query to inspect later outcomes.

functions.name: batch-trigger-workflows
functions.description: Submit one configured workflow for multiple users and/or devices with shared parameters. Accept up to 100 users and 100 devices and return aggregate request and execution IDs.

users.description: User target identifiers, up to 100; omitted maps to an empty array.

upn.description: User principal name in the provider-supported email-like form.

items.description: User target with at least one identifier; multiple identifier fields are preserved.

devices.description: Device target identifiers, up to 100; omitted maps to an empty array. No positional pairing with users is promised.

name.description: Device name; ambiguous matches select the most recently active device.

collectorId.description: Collector UUID mapped to collectorUid, distinct from the inventory UID.

items.description: Device target with at least one identifier; multiple identifier fields are preserved.

parameters.description: Shared workflow parameter values; omitted sends an empty map.

workflowId.description: NQL ID of the one workflow to start for these targets.

users.description: User target identifiers, up to 100; omitted maps to an empty array.

devices.description: Device target identifiers, up to 100; omitted maps to an empty array. No positional pairing with users is promised.

FunctionInput_nexthink_batchtriggerworkf.description: One workflow and shared parameters for a nonempty batch of up to 100 users and 100 devices.

requestId.description: Shared request identifier for the spawned workflow executions.

items.description: Provider-reported workflow execution identifier.

executionIds.description: Provider-reported execution identifiers, without invented input correlation, per-target success or completion claims.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_batchtriggerwork.description: Aggregate identifiers acknowledging workflow submission, not execution completion.

tags.instructions: Get an API-triggerable workflow NQL ID and its dependency with `list-workflows` or `get-workflow`. Use `trigger-workflow` for one target, one user-device context, or a targetless workflow. Maximum 100 users and 100 devices per call; supply at least one target. Do not assume positional user/device pairing or per-target completion. Ambiguous external identifiers select the most recently active match. Workflow effects may be destructive and replay may repeat them.

functions.name: batch-update-inventory-objects
functions.description: Apply partial enrichment updates to up to 100 inventory objects in one native request, preserving the provider's aggregate status and object-specific error reports.

domain.description: Enrichment source/domain label shared by the request, primarily for tracking.

field.description: Supported identity field selecting this object's resource type.

value.description: Exact identity value, retained as an opaque string.

target.description: One field/value identity for this object; identities must be distinct within the batch.

additionalProperties.description: Literal string or integer enrichment value; null is unsupported.

fields.description: Partial field updates keyed by supported enrichment paths. Omitted fields remain outside the update; empty string is literal, null is rejected, and date-valued fields use YYYY-MM-DD strings.

items.description: One inventory object identity and its partial enrichment updates.

objects.description: Up to 100 object updates. The public maximum is deliberately below the documented intended native 10,000-object limit.

FunctionInput_nexthink_batchupdateinvent.description: A shared enrichment domain and a bounded batch of partial inventory object updates.

status.description: Provider aggregate processing status; does not imply atomicity or per-field rollback.

errors.description: Only object errors explicitly reported by Nexthink; omitted when no errors are returned. No individual success records are invented.

field.description: Identification field returned for the object with errors.

value.description: Identification value returned for the object with errors.

target.description: Provider identification of the object with errors; not a fabricated input-position success report.

code.description: Provider's individual enrichment error code, unchanged.

items.description: An individual enrichment error reported by the provider.

errors.description: Reported errors for this object; correct field/type/identity issues using the provider detail before retrying.

items.description: Provider-reported identification and errors for an inventory object.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_batchupdateinven.description: The provider aggregate enrichment result and any explicitly reported object errors.

tags.instructions: Use `update-inventory-object` for one object. Provide up to 100 objects with one identification field/value each and supported enrichment field paths. Obtain object identifiers through saved queries using `execute-nql-query`. Only supplied fields are updated; null clearing is unsupported. Results can be partial and are not atomic. Inspect errors before retrying, and do not assume errors imply every field was unchanged.

functions.name: execute-nql-query
functions.description: Execute a saved, optionally parameterized NQL query and return directly usable result rows. Synchronous execution returns at most 1,000 rows and is not a complete inventory export.

logTag.description: Optional categorization tag stored in Nexthink platform logs; do not include sensitive data.

queryId.description: ID of a saved NQL API query configured in this Nexthink instance, including its leading #.

parameters.description: Named substitution values for the saved query. Omit to send no substitutions; empty strings are preserved.

additionalProperties.description: A substitution value, passed unchanged to the saved query.

FunctionInput_nexthink_executenqlquery.description: Execute one saved NQL API query with optional named substitutions and a platform log tag.

additionalProperties.description: The original JSON cell value, without type coercion.

items.description: One result row keyed by the original NQL column names.
Query result rows keyed by NQL column name. Values retain their JSON types; numeric-looking identifiers and opaque strings are not coerced.

queryId.description: ID of the query that was executed, when returned.

rowCount.description: Provider-reported number of rows in this result, not the total number of matching inventory objects.

executedAt.description: Execution instant normalized to UTC with Z, when returned.

executedQuery.description: Final NQL source after parameter substitution, when returned.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_executenqlquery.description: A single bounded synchronous NQL result, with optional provider execution metadata and no continuation token.

nqlApiVersion.description: Deployment compatibility override. Omit for V2; select V1 only for a legacy deployment.

tags.instructions: Obtain the saved query ID from Administration > NQL API queries; this tool does not accept arbitrary NQL source. Use it for small lookups, including execution tracking. Use `start-nql-export` for larger datasets, then `get-nql-export` to check that export. There is no continuation token for the synchronous result.

functions.name: get-nql-export
functions.description: Get an export's current state and, when ready, its temporary result-file URL. Explicitly identify results truncated by the license limit.

exportId.description: Opaque identifier returned when the export was submitted.

FunctionInput_nexthink_getnqlexport.description: Identifier of the NQL export whose current state should be retrieved.

id.description: Export identifier supplied for this lookup.

status.description: Current export lifecycle state; ERROR is a job outcome rather than a successful file.

truncated.description: True when the status response reports that license limits truncated the query results.

downloadUrl.description: Temporary result-file URL when returned; valid for 15 minutes after generation. Omitted when absent or null.

errorDescription.description: Provider's export failure explanation when present; omitted for absent or null values.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_getnqlexport.description: Current NQL export state, license-truncation flag, and available file URL or failure explanation.

tags.instructions: Use the id returned by `start-nql-export`. Each call checks status once; if still submitted or in progress, check again later rather than starting another export. Download a ready file promptly: the URL is valid for 15 minutes after generation. A GZIP or ZSTD file must be decompressed after downloading. Inspect truncated before treating a result as complete.

functions.name: get-remote-action

functions.name: hand-off-conversation-to-spark

Identifies an exact-byte file message part.

mimeType.description: Media type describing the file bytes, for example application/pdf.

items.description: A text or file message part.

parts.description: Message parts in display order; text is ordinary text and file content preserves exact bytes.

This initiates a conversation handoff; it does not return Spark's reply or prove the user received it. File parts contain exact bytes represented as base64, not encoded ordinary text. Repeating the handoff may create duplicate interactions.

functions.name: schedule-device-deletion

Inspect the returned status before assuming the device was queued, and do not blindly replay an ambiguous request.

A request ID establishes request creation, not display, response or delivery; inspect per-user rejection messages. Repeating the call can create new campaign requests.

functions.name: update-inventory-object
functions.description: Enrich selected supported fields on one device, user, binary or package. This is a partial field update, not replacement of the entire inventory object.

domain.description: Caller's enrichment source/domain label used primarily for information and tracking.

field.description: Supported field used to identify the object's resource and identity.

value.description: Exact identifier value for the selected identification field; kept opaque and not numerically coerced.

target.description: One identification field and value selecting the inventory object.

additionalProperties.description: Desired string or integer value, preserved without conversion.

fields.description: Supported enrichment field paths mapped to desired string or integer values. Omitted fields are unchanged; null is rejected; empty string is sent literally, not treated as omission. Date-valued fields use YYYY-MM-DD strings without timezone conversion.

FunctionInput_nexthink_updateinventoryob.description: The enrichment domain, one inventory object identifier, and the explicit fields to update.

status.description: Whether Nexthink processed this object's enrichment successfully; error does not imply rollback of already applied fields.

errors.description: Object-specific provider failures, when reported; omitted when none are returned.

code.description: Provider's object-specific enrichment error code, retained verbatim.

items.description: One object-specific enrichment failure reported by Nexthink.

FunctionOutput_nexthink_updateinventoryo.description: The enrichment outcome for the selected object, including any reported object-specific errors.

tags.instructions: Use a known object identifier, obtainable with a saved query through `execute-nql-query`, and field paths from the Nexthink enrichment configuration. Supported fields are manual custom fields, device configuration/virtualization fields and supported user directory/organization fields. Use `batch-update-inventory-objects` for several objects. Only supplied fields are changed; null clearing is not supported by this contract. Check the result for object-specific errors.
